commitments.quote: It applies to all agreements under which Business Associate creates, receives, maintains or transmits Protected Health Information for or on behalf of Covered Entity (the "Underlying Agreements").
commitments.summary: The BAA applies to every agreement under which ExampleCo handles PHI for Amazing Health System and its affiliated hospitals and clinics.
commitments.scope: All Underlying Agreements involving PHI of Amazing Health System and its affiliated hospitals and clinics.
commitments.deviation: The DPA says it controls over the Agreement as to processing of Customer Personal Data. The BAA has no order-of-precedence clause and does not address the DPA. Inference: if both documents apply to the same data, which notice period controls (DPA 72 hours after confirmation versus BAA 10 days after Discovery or 5 business days after awareness) is not resolved by either document's text.

commitments.quote: "Security Incident" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity.
commitments.summary: Security Incidents that trigger reporting are limited to incidents involving ePHI handled by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors for Covered Entity.
commitments.scope: Attempted or successful unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification or destruction of information, or interference with system operations (45 C.F.R. § 164.304), involving ePHI only, including incidents at Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: The DPA's Personal Data Breach requires ExampleCo confirmation of an actual compromise and excludes unsuccessful attempts. The HIPAA definition covers attempted as well as successful incidents and does not require confirmation, but it is limited to electronic PHI.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as permitted by this BAA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may use and disclose PHI only to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as the BAA permits.
commitments.scope: All PHI, including limited data sets (Section 2.4).
commitments.deviation: The DPA limits processing to Customer's documented instructions. The BAA limits use and disclosure to performance, legal requirement or BAA permission. The type is the closest available; the term is a general use limitation, not specific to AI.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.scope: All PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no minimum-necessary standard.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may de-identify PHI only by the HIPAA safe harbor method and may use the result only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.scope: PHI de-identified by ExampleCo.
commitments.deviation: DPA 8.2 lets ExampleCo use aggregated or de-identified Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services, with no prescribed de-identification method. The BAA requires the safe harbor method only (expert determination is not allowed) and limits use to providing and improving the services under the Underlying Agreements.

commitments.quote: Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
commitments.summary: Information de-identified under the safe harbor method in Section 2.3 is outside the BAA.
commitments.scope: Only information de-identified by the safe harbor method falls outside the BAA. Inference: information de-identified any other way remains PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA's Usage Data carve-out covers any aggregated or de-identified data that does not identify Customer or any person. The BAA carve-out is narrower and depends on safe harbor compliance.

commitments.quote: A limited data set under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) is PHI for all purposes of this BAA.
commitments.summary: Limited data sets are treated as PHI for every purpose of the BAA.
commitments.scope: Limited data sets under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e).
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no equivalent. Inference: under the DPA, partially de-identified data might fall within Usage Data. The BAA expressly keeps limited data sets inside all its protections.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to ePHI.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must comply with the HIPAA Security Rule for ePHI.
commitments.scope: ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits to Annex 2 Security Measures, which ExampleCo may update unilaterally. The BAA requires compliance with the HIPAA Security Rule, an external regulatory standard ExampleCo cannot change.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must not store or process PHI outside the United States.
commitments.scope: All PHI, including limited data sets. Inference: this also binds Subcontractors through the flow-down in Section 5.1.
commitments.deviation: The DPA stores data at rest in the region the customer selects. The BAA imposes a fixed US-only restriction on storage and on all processing, not only storage at rest.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must not access PHI from outside the United States.
commitments.scope: All PHI. Inference: this extends to Subcontractors through Section 5.1.
commitments.deviation: The DPA permits access from outside the hosting region for support, maintenance and security, including from the Manila, Philippines support center. The BAA prohibits any access to PHI from outside the US, so offshore support access to PHI is not allowed.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall maintain HITRUST r2 certification for the systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain HITRUST r2 certification for systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.scope: Systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits to SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001 or substantially equivalent successors. The BAA requires HITRUST r2 specifically and allows no successor substitution.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and no later than 10 calendar days after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery of the Breach. Under the HIPAA definition incorporated by Section 1.1 (45 C.F.R. § 164.410(a)(2)), this is the first day the Breach is known to ExampleCo, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any ExampleCo workforce member or agent other than the person committing it.

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4), in writing.
commitments.scope: Breaches of Unsecured PHI in any form (not only electronic), including limited data sets.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires notice within 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a breach. The BAA allows 10 calendar days, a longer period, but starts the clock at Discovery, which includes constructive knowledge by any workforce member or agent, not ExampleCo's confirmation. There is no confirmation step.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any Security Incident within 5 business days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo becoming aware of the Security Incident (actual awareness by Business Associate).

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4), in writing.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents involving ePHI handled by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors (Section 1.2), including attempted incidents, except unsuccessful attempts covered by the standing notice. Inference: a Breach of ePHI will usually also be a Security Incident, so this shorter period may require an initial report before the Section 4.1 deadline.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has a single 72-hour deadline after confirmation of a Personal Data Breach and excludes unconfirmed or attempted incidents. The BAA adds a separate 5 business day duty for Security Incidents, including unconfirmed ones, triggered by awareness.

commitments.quote: This Section 4.2 serves as notice of, and no further report is required for, unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.summary: Section 4.2 itself serves as standing notice of unsuccessful attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI, so no separate report is required for them.
commitments.scope: Unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA excludes unsuccessful attempts from the breach definition entirely. The BAA treats them as Security Incidents but deems them already reported. Denial-of-service attacks are not expressly listed, unlike in the DPA.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any use or disclosure of PHI not permitted by the BAA within 10 calendar days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo becoming aware of the non-permitted use or disclosure.

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4), in writing.
commitments.scope: Any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by the BAA, whether or not it is a Breach or Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no separate duty to report non-permitted uses or disclosures that fall short of a confirmed breach.

commitments.quote: Reports under this Section 4 shall be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example.
commitments.summary: All Section 4 reports must be in writing to the Privacy Office, with a copy to the Information Security Office.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example.
commitments.scope: All reports under Sections 4.1 to 4.3.
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the security contact designated in the admin console, or otherwise to the account owner. The BAA fixes two named email addresses, requires written reports, and requires a copy to the ISO.

commitments.quote: A report of a Breach shall include, to the extent known, the identity of each individual affected, the PHI involved, the date of the Breach and of its Discovery, and the steps taken to mitigate it.
commitments.summary: Breach reports must include, to the extent known, each affected individual's identity, the PHI involved, the dates of the Breach and of its Discovery, and mitigation steps.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to iso@ahs.example.
commitments.scope: Reports of Breaches of Unsecured PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires the nature of the breach, categories of data and measures taken. The BAA requires identification of each affected individual and the breach and Discovery dates. Unlike DPA 7.3, the BAA states no express duty to provide further information as it becomes available.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors.
commitments.scope: Breaches caused by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors. The costs covered are notification to individuals, regulators and the media.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA's only related term (7.4) says notification is not an acknowledgment of fault, and the DPA has no cost reimbursement.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must ensure that each Subcontractor handling PHI agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions as ExampleCo.
commitments.scope: Each Subcontractor (45 C.F.R. § 160.103) that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI for ExampleCo. Inference: this includes AI model providers and offshore support vendors that touch PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes ExampleCo responsible for Subprocessors' performance. The BAA requires a written flow-down of identical terms, including the US-only and 5-day and 10-day reporting duties. The BAA contains no Subcontractor notice or objection mechanism comparable to DPA 5.2 to 5.4.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within ten (10) business days after Covered Entity's request, so Covered Entity can meet 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within 10 business days after a request.

deadline.anchor: Covered Entity's request

commitments.scope: PHI in a Designated Record Set. This is the closest available type; the term concerns individual access rights.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of determining compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the HHS Secretary for compliance review.
commitments.recipient: Secretary of Health and Human Services
commitments.scope: Internal practices, books and records relating to PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA limits audits to Trust Center reports, plus one on-site audit per 12 months on 60 days' notice when a supervisory authority requires it. The BAA grants HHS access with no frequency, notice or cost limits.

commitments.quote: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, Business Associate shall return or destroy all PHI within thirty (30) days.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must return or destroy all PHI within 30 days after termination of the Underlying Agreements.

deadline.anchor: Termination of the Underlying Agreements

commitments.scope: All PHI, including limited data sets. There is no express carve-out for backups.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows 90 days to delete, plus a further 35 days for backup overwrite, and provides certification only on request. The BAA requires return or destruction of all PHI within 30 days, with no separate backup period.

commitments.quote: If return or destruction is not feasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.summary: If return or destruction is not feasible, ExampleCo must keep applying the BAA's protections to any retained PHI for as long as it keeps it.
commitments.scope: PHI whose return or destruction is not feasible.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no infeasibility provision or post-termination continuation of protections.

commitments.quote: This Addendum controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement, any order form, and any data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document published or provided by Supplier.
commitments.summary: The Addendum overrides any conflicting Supplier document, including ExampleCo's standard DPA, for every duty it covers, such as incident notice, subcontractors, data location, AI and audit.
commitments.scope: Conflicts between this Addendum and the Agreement, order forms, and any Supplier DPA, privacy policy or other Supplier document.
commitments.deviation: Reverses the DPA's precedence rule. The DPA says it controls over the Agreement for processing; here the Bank Addendum controls over the DPA itself, so DPA terms such as the 72-hour confirmed-breach notice, 30-day subprocessor notice and Manila support access give way where they conflict.

commitments.quote: Terms incorporated by reference to a Supplier website, including any Supplier trust or security site, do not bind Bank and do not modify this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Terms on Supplier's websites, including its Trust Center, do not bind Bank or change this Addendum.
commitments.scope: Any term incorporated by reference to a Supplier website or trust/security site, including the Trust Center subprocessor list, Trust Center NDA terms and Trust Center-based notices.
commitments.deviation: The DPA relies on the Trust Center for subprocessor lists and notices (5.1, 5.2), report access (9.1, 9.2) and AI provider disclosure (8.3). None of these Trust Center mechanisms binds Bank.

commitments.quote: "Bank Data" means all data and information, in any form, that Supplier or any Subcontractor receives, accesses, creates or processes in connection with the Agreement, including (a) data provided by or on behalf of Bank or its customers; (b) metadata, logs and configuration data relating to Bank's use of the Services; and (c) any data derived from any of the foregoing, including model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and data that has been aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized.
commitments.summary: Bank Data covers all data handled in connection with the Agreement, including metadata, logs, model outputs, embeddings, annotations and aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized derivatives.
commitments.scope: Every duty that applies to Bank Data, including the encryption, residency, AI-use, incident, deletion and subcontractor duties, extends to derived, aggregated and de-identified data and to usage metadata and logs.
commitments.deviation: The DPA covers only Customer Personal Data and lets ExampleCo use aggregated or de-identified Usage Data to improve the Services (1.6, 8.2). Here aggregated and de-identified data remain Bank Data, so there is no Usage Data carve-out and the protections are not limited to personal data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a written information security program that is consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the FFIEC Information Technology Examination Handbook.
commitments.summary: Supplier must maintain a written security program consistent with the NIST CSF and the FFIEC IT Examination Handbook.
commitments.deviation: The DPA refers only to the Annex 2 measures, which ExampleCo may update unilaterally. This term requires a written program aligned to the named NIST and FFIEC frameworks.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data at rest using AES-256 or stronger and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Supplier must encrypt Bank Data at rest with AES-256 or stronger and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data, including derived and de-identified data.
commitments.deviation: The encryption standard matches Annex 2. It applies to the broader Bank Data and is a fixed contractual duty rather than a measure ExampleCo can update.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.summary: Supplier must require MFA for all remote access to systems handling Bank Data.
commitments.scope: All remote access to any system that stores, processes or transmits Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires MFA for access to production systems. This term covers all remote access to any system handling Bank Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall complete a criminal background check on all Supplier Personnel before granting them access to Bank Data, to the extent permitted by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier must run criminal background checks on all Supplier and Subcontractor personnel before they access Bank Data, where the law permits.
commitments.scope: Supplier Personnel, meaning employees, contractors and agents of Supplier and of any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain throughout the term of the Agreement a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services for the whole term.
commitments.deviation: Requires a current SOC 2 Type II report with no option to substitute a successor standard. ISO/IEC 27001 is not required.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall store and process Bank Data only within the United States.
commitments.summary: Supplier must store and process Bank Data only in the United States.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data, covering both storage and processing.
commitments.deviation: The DPA fixes only at-rest storage, in the customer-selected region. This term requires both storage and processing to stay in the US.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any Supplier Personnel located outside the United States to access Bank Data, including for support or maintenance, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.summary: No Supplier or Subcontractor personnel outside the US may access Bank Data, including for support, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.scope: Supplier Personnel, including Subcontractor personnel, located outside the US.
commitments.deviation: The DPA permits offshore support, maintenance and security access, including from the Manila support center. This term prohibits offshore access without prior written approval, so routine Manila support for Bank would breach it.

commitments.quote: Supplier may permit only the Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 ("Approved Subcontractors") to access Bank Data, and each only within the scope stated for it in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: Only the Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 may access Bank Data, and each only within its stated scope.
commitments.scope: Subcontractor is defined to include Supplier Affiliates and any third party that has access to Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: Replaces the DPA's general authorization and Trust Center list with a closed list in which each Subcontractor has a defined scope. Supplier Affiliates are covered as well.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give Bank's Third-Party Risk Management office at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice, delivered as provided in Exhibit C, before adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.summary: Supplier must give at least 90 days' prior written notice to Bank's TPRM office before adding, replacing or expanding the scope of any Subcontractor.

deadline.anchor: Adding or replacing any Subcontractor, or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope

commitments.recipient: Bank Third-Party Risk Management office, tprm-notices@anb.example, with a copy to Awesome National Bank, N.A., Legal Department, 100 Example Plaza, New York, NY 10001 (Exhibit C)
commitments.scope: New Subcontractors, replacement Subcontractors, and expansions of an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.deviation: Requires 90 days' notice instead of 30, delivered directly to TPRM with a copy to Legal rather than by a Trust Center update or email to subscribers. Scope expansions also trigger notice, and there is no emergency-replacement exception like DPA 5.4.

commitments.quote: Bank may object within thirty (30) days after receiving the notice. If Bank objects, Supplier shall not engage the Subcontractor for the Services provided to Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
commitments.summary: Bank may object within 30 days for any reason; if it does, Supplier must not use that Subcontractor for Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services with a pro-rata refund.

deadline.anchor: Bank's receipt of the Subcontractor notice

commitments.deviation: The DPA allows objection only on reasonable data protection grounds within 15 days, with termination as the sole remedy. Here Bank has 30 days with no grounds requirement, Supplier is barred from using the Subcontractor for Bank, and termination comes with no penalty and a pro-rata refund.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall impose on each Subcontractor written obligations at least as protective of Bank Data as this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Supplier must flow down written obligations at least as protective as this Addendum to every Subcontractor.
commitments.scope: All Subcontractors, including Supplier Affiliates.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within six (6) hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must contractually require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within 6 hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.

deadline.anchor: The Subcontractor's Discovery, meaning the earliest time the Subcontractor knew or reasonably should have known of the Security Incident

commitments.scope: Security Incidents, including suspected incidents and unauthorized access to Subcontractor systems.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier remains fully liable to Bank for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Supplier is fully liable for its Subcontractors' acts and omissions.
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes ExampleCo responsible for its Subprocessors' performance of DPA obligations. This term imposes full liability for all of a Subcontractor's acts and omissions.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and in no event later than twelve (12) hours after Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and within 12 hours after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery, meaning the earliest time Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or with reasonable diligence would have known, of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center, telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147 and email cfc-thirdparty@anb.example (Exhibit C)
commitments.scope: Security Incidents: actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration or destruction of, Bank Data, and unauthorized access to any Supplier or Subcontractor system handling Bank Data, whether or not data access is confirmed.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a breach of personal data. This term allows 12 hours, the clock starts at actual or constructive knowledge by Supplier or any Subcontractor, and suspected incidents and system intrusions count even without confirmed data access.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give notice under Section 6.1 by telephone and by email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center as provided in Exhibit C. Notice provided only to Bank's relationship manager, or through a Supplier status page or trust site, does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Incident notice must go by both telephone and email to the Cyber Fusion Center; notice only to the relationship manager, a status page or a trust site does not count.
commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center, telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147 and email cfc-thirdparty@anb.example. The relationship manager, Dana Okafor (dana.okafor@anb.example), is for routine matters only (Exhibit C).
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the console-designated security contact or the account owner. This term requires dual-channel notice to a fixed Bank Cyber Fusion Center and excludes the relationship manager and status or trust pages.

commitments.quote: Supplier's initial notice shall include all information then known about the Security Incident, including the date and time of Discovery, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected.
commitments.summary: The initial notice must include all known information, including the Discovery time, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the categories of Bank Data affected.
commitments.deviation: Requires all known information plus specific items (Discovery time, systems, Subcontractors, potentially affected data). The DPA requires only the nature of the breach, the data categories and the measures taken.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall provide written status updates at least once every twenty-four (24) hours until the Security Incident is contained
commitments.summary: Supplier must send written status updates at least every 24 hours until the incident is contained.

deadline.anchor: From initial notice until the Security Incident is contained

commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center (Exhibit C), by inference as the Section 6 incident contact
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires further information only as it becomes available. This term requires a written update at least every 24 hours.

commitments.quote: and shall deliver a written root-cause report within thirty (30) days after containment.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver a written root-cause report within 30 days after containment.

deadline.anchor: Containment of the Security Incident

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not notify any Bank customer, regulator, law enforcement agency or the media of a Security Incident involving Bank Data without Bank's prior written consent, unless required by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not tell Bank customers, regulators, law enforcement or the media about an incident without Bank's written consent, unless the law requires it.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents involving Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Where law requires such notice, Supplier shall inform Bank before giving it, to the extent legally permitted.
commitments.summary: Where the law requires third-party notice, Supplier must tell Bank before giving it, where legally permitted.

deadline.anchor: Supplier giving a legally required notice to a third party

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall preserve all logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident for at least one (1) year after containment
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep all forensic evidence of a Security Incident for at least one year after containment.

deadline.anchor: Containment of the Security Incident

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: and shall give Bank and its designated forensic investigator access to that evidence on request.
commitments.summary: Supplier must give Bank and its forensic investigator access to the preserved evidence on request.
commitments.recipient: Bank and its designated forensic investigator
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall reimburse Bank's reasonable costs of investigating and responding to a Security Incident caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor, including costs of notifying affected individuals and providing them with twenty-four (24) months of credit monitoring.
commitments.summary: Supplier must reimburse Bank's reasonable investigation and response costs for incidents caused by Supplier or a Subcontractor, including individual notice and 24 months of credit monitoring.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Where this Addendum, the Agreement, any exhibit or schedule, or applicable law specifies more than one period for the same notice, the shortest period applies.
commitments.summary: Where more than one period applies to the same notice, the shortest one governs.
commitments.scope: Competing notice periods across the Addendum, Agreement, exhibits, schedules and law. The 12-hour period in 6.1 therefore displaces the 72-hour period in Exhibit D.2 and the DPA's 72-hour period.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any artificial intelligence or machine learning model, other than a model used solely to provide the Services to Bank.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any AI model except one used solely to serve Bank.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data, including aggregated, de-identified and derived data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA bars only training or fine-tuning of foundation models offered to other customers, and 8.2 allows Usage Data to improve the Services. This term bars training, fine-tuning, evaluation and improvement of any model other than a Bank-only model, and it covers de-identified data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any person to review, label or annotate Bank Data for the purpose of developing or improving any model, except as expressly permitted for an Approved Subcontractor in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: No person may review, label or annotate Bank Data for model development except as Schedule 2 expressly permits.
commitments.scope: The only Schedule 2 exception is Labelforge, for de-identified feedback samples.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall identify in Schedule 2 every third-party model provider that receives Bank Data
commitments.summary: Every third-party model provider receiving Bank Data must be listed in Schedule 2.
commitments.deviation: Model providers must appear in the contractual Schedule 2 rather than on the Trust Center list.

commitments.quote: and shall ensure that no model provider retains Bank Data after returning a response.
commitments.summary: Supplier must ensure no model provider retains Bank Data after returning a response.
commitments.deviation: Requires zero retention with no abuse-monitoring exception, and Supplier must ensure the result rather than merely require it of providers.

commitments.quote: Bank, its auditors and its regulators may audit Supplier's compliance with this Addendum once in any twelve (12) month period on thirty (30) days' written notice, and at any time after a Security Incident on five (5) business days' written notice.

commitments.summary: Supplier must test the BC/DR plan at least annually and give Bank a summary of the results.

Inference: this means ExampleCo's 72-hour, confirmation-based breach clock does not govern notice to Retailer, and the VDPA's 24-hour, awareness-based clock in 6.1 does.
commitments.deviation: The DPA says the DPA controls over the Agreement for processing of Customer Personal Data. The VDPA instead makes Retailer's own terms prevail over all Vendor and Affiliate data processing terms, which would include the ExampleCo DPA itself.

commitments.quote: "Retailer Data" means all data that Retailer, its employees or its customers provide to Vendor or that Vendor collects from Retailer's systems, including telemetry, logs, traces and metrics, and all data derived from any of it.
commitments.summary: Protected Retailer Data includes all provided or collected data, expressly covering telemetry, logs, traces, metrics and all derived data.
commitments.scope: Covers all data, not only personal data, including operational telemetry and any derived (including aggregated or de-identified) data. It therefore governs the use limits in 3.2, residency in 3.3, incident scope in 2.3/6.1 and deletion in 7.1.
commitments.deviation: The DPA covers only Customer Personal Data. It carves out aggregated or de-identified 'Usage Data', which ExampleCo may use to operate, secure and improve the Services (DPA 8.2). The VDPA treats telemetry and all derived data as Retailer Data, so there is no Usage Data carve-out.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall process Retailer Data only to provide the services described in the Subscription Agreement (the "Services") and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.summary: Vendor may process Retailer Data only to provide the Services and only on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data, including telemetry and derived data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA treats the Agreement, the DPA and Customer's configuration of the Services as instructions, and applies only to personal data. The VDPA limits processing to providing the Services on written instructions and covers all Retailer Data.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model, except models used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.summary: Vendor must not use Retailer Data to train or improve any ML model unless the model is used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data, including telemetry and derived data. Inference: this also applies to ExampleCo's AI features, because ExampleCo is an approved Subprocessor for AI features and 5.3 requires flow-down of equally protective terms.
commitments.deviation: The DPA bars training or fine-tuning only of foundation models made available to other customers, and it permits use of Usage Data to improve the Services. The VDPA bars training or improving any model except one dedicated to Retailer, and it has no Usage Data exception.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.

It does not expressly address offshore access. Inference: Manila support access under ExampleCo's DPA is not authorized by the VDPA, and its permissibility depends on the processing limits in 3.1 and 5.3.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards that meet or exceed the CIS Critical Security Controls, Implementation Group 2.
commitments.summary: Vendor must maintain safeguards meeting or exceeding CIS Critical Security Controls IG2.
commitments.deviation: The DPA refers to its own Annex 2 measures, which ExampleCo may update unilaterally provided overall security is not materially reduced. The VDPA sets an external benchmark (CIS IG2) and gives Vendor no unilateral right to change it.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.summary: Vendor must encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA specifies AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit. The VDPA requires 'industry-standard' encryption without naming algorithms; the substance is similar but less specific.

commitments.summary: Vendor must obtain a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services every year.

commitments.summary: Vendor must deliver the SOC 2 Type II report to Retailer within 15 days of Retailer's request.

commitments.summary: Vendor must contractually bind each Subprocessor to obligations at least as protective as the VDPA.

commitments.summary: Breach notices go to Customer's designated security contact in the administration console, or to the account owner if none is designated.
commitments.recipient: Security contact designated in the Services administration console; fallback to Customer's account owner

commitments.quote: ExampleCo's notice will describe, to the extent then known, the nature of the Personal Data Breach, the categories of data affected, and the measures taken or proposed to address it. ExampleCo will provide further information as it becomes available.
commitments.summary: The breach notice must describe, as far as then known, the nature of the breach, the data categories affected and the remedial measures, and ExampleCo must provide further information as it becomes available.
commitments.recipient: Security contact designated in the Services administration console, or account owner

commitments.quote: ExampleCo's notification of or response to a Personal Data Breach is not an acknowledgment of fault or liability.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo's breach notification or response does not count as an admission of fault or liability.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune any foundation model that is made available to other customers.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune any foundation model made available to other customers.
commitments.scope: Covers all Customer Data, not only Customer Personal Data. Inference: the restriction does not expressly cover models that are not foundation models or models not made available to other customers.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo may use Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may use Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.
commitments.scope: Usage Data means aggregated or de-identified data about the use and performance of the Services that does not identify Customer or any natural person. It is outside Customer Personal Data and the 8.1 restriction.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo lists the third-party model providers used by AI features as Subprocessors on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: Third-party AI model providers are treated as Subprocessors and listed on the Trust Center.
commitments.scope: Third-party model providers used by AI features.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo requires its model providers not to retain prompts or outputs beyond the time needed to return a response, except as required for abuse monitoring.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must require its model providers not to retain prompts or outputs beyond the time needed to return a response, except as required for abuse monitoring.
commitments.scope: Prompts and outputs of AI features; abuse-monitoring retention is carved out.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will make its most recent SOC 2 Type II report available to Customer through the Trust Center, subject to Customer's acceptance of the Trust Center non-disclosure terms.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make its latest SOC 2 Type II report available through the Trust Center once Customer accepts the non-disclosure terms.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will engage an independent third party to perform a penetration test of the Services at least annually and will make an executive summary of the results available through the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must have an independent third party penetration-test the Services at least annually and publish an executive summary on the Trust Center.

deadline.anchor: previous penetration test

commitments.scope: Only an executive summary is provided, not full results.

commitments.quote: Customer agrees that the reports in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 satisfy any audit right under Data Protection Laws.
commitments.summary: Customer accepts that the SOC 2 report and the penetration test summary satisfy its statutory audit rights.

commitments.quote: Where a supervisory authority requires a further audit, Customer may conduct one on-site audit per twelve (12) month period, with at least sixty (60) days' written notice, during business hours, and at Customer's expense.
commitments.summary: If a supervisory authority requires it, Customer may conduct one on-site audit every 12 months, on at least 60 days' written notice, during business hours and at its own expense.

deadline.anchor: the on-site audit

secondary_deadline.anchor: one on-site audit per twelve-month period

commitments.scope: Available only where a supervisory authority requires a further audit.

commitments.quote: Within ninety (90) days after termination or expiry of the Agreement, ExampleCo will delete Customer Personal Data from the Services. Backups are overwritten in the ordinary course within a further thirty-five (35) days.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must delete Customer Personal Data from the Services within 90 days after termination or expiry, and backups are overwritten within a further 35 days.

deadline.anchor: termination or expiry of the Agreement

secondary_deadline.anchor: end of the 90-day deletion period (backup overwrite)

commitments.scope: Customer Personal Data in the Services and backups.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will provide written certification of deletion upon Customer's written request.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must provide written certification of deletion when Customer requests it in writing.

commitments.quote: If this DPA conflicts with the Agreement, this DPA controls as to the processing of Customer Personal Data.
commitments.summary: Where the DPA conflicts with the Agreement, the DPA controls on the processing of Customer Personal Data.
commitments.scope: Limited to the processing of Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: Customer Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Customer Data must be encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.scope: All Customer Data.

commitments.quote: Access to production systems requires multi-factor authentication.
commitments.summary: Access to production systems must require multi-factor authentication.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo maintains a business continuity and disaster recovery plan and tests it at least annually.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan and test it at least annually.

deadline.anchor: previous plan test

rejected.quote: Amendment No. 1 to Appendix B (September 8, 2025), added: ExampleCo, Inc. (Vendor Affiliate) | Platform hosting and AI features for the Services | United States
rejected.summary: ExampleCo, a Vendor Affiliate, was approved on September 8, 2025 as a Subprocessor for platform hosting and AI features, located in the United States.
rejected.scope: Approval is limited to platform hosting and AI features, with a United States location. Inference: ExampleCo's Manila support access and third-party AI model providers allowed under its DPA (6.2, 8.3) fall outside this approval and would need separate consent under 5.1. ExampleCo remains bound by 3.2 and 6.1 through 5.3 and 1.1.
rejected.deviation: Under its own DPA, ExampleCo would operate under general authorization with offshore access and model-provider subprocessors. Here it is approved only for named purposes in a US location, subject to VDPA terms.
